<reason>B more convincingly isolated the motion’s decisive burden: why mandatory governmental approval adds safety beyond independently verified, enforceable pre-release requirements. A established that irreversible diffusion warrants prevention, but repeatedly mischaracterized B’s preventive regime as self-certification and after-the-fact punishment. B answered both pressure questions directly, preserved investigative and blocking powers, and explained the distinct competitive cost of approval queues. A’s deadline exception further weakened its claim that only completed clearance makes safeguards binding. This was a solid win on comparative necessity, not a rejection of stringent AI oversight.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B’s strongest exchange distinguished mandatory independent verification from mandatory governmental permission, then tested that distinction against A’s provisional-deployment exception. If safeguards remain binding while approval is unfinished, A cannot simply assert that the approval gate uniquely enables prevention. A’s closing repeated that assertion rather than resolving the challenge.</best_rebuttal>
